claims.text: Sit with the back against the pad, the thigh pads against the inner thighs just above the knees, feet on the footrests, and hold the side handles.

quotes.text: Sit on the hip adduction machine with back against the pad, adjust thigh pads against inner thighs above knees, feet on footrests, and grip side handles.
Adjust the machine to the appropriate settings, sit down with your legs outside the pads, and grip the handles.

claims.text: Start with the legs spread only to a light stretch in the inner thighs; avoid an excessive stretch at the start.

quotes.text: Start with legs spread to feel a light stretch in inner thighs; adduct until pads lightly touch without forcing.
Avoid excessive stretch in starting position

claims.text: Squeeze the thighs together until the pads nearly or lightly touch, pause briefly, then return slowly while keeping tension.

quotes.text: Exhale and squeeze thighs together to bring pads inward until they nearly touch.
Pause briefly at peak contraction to engage inner thighs.
Inhale and slowly return legs to starting position, maintaining tension.

claims.text: Keep the spine neutral and the back flat against the pad; avoid momentum.

quotes.text: Keep spine neutral and avoid using momentum.

claims.text: Don't use the machine with an acute hip or groin injury; choose a moderate weight and make sure the selector pin is secure.

quotes.text: Do not use if acute hip or groin injury present

claims.text: Breathe out as the thighs squeeze together and in on the return.

quotes.text: Inhale during the return to start; exhale as you squeeze thighs together.

claims.text: The machine isolates the inner-thigh adductors (Motra names adductor longus and magnus).

quotes.text: Seated machine exercise isolating inner thigh adductors

claims.text: Measured in 16 untrained women: the adduction machine recruited the hip adductors about as well as elastic-band adduction.

quotes.text: Although elastic resistance and exercise machine seem equally effective for recruiting muscle activity of the hip adductors,

claims.text: Tempo: about 2 s in, a 1 s pause, 2 s out.

quotes.text: at a moderate contraction velocity (1-2 s CON; 1-2 s ECC)

claims.text: Load progression: add 2-10% load once you can do one or two reps more than the target number.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

plate.viewWhy: The legs move together in the frontal plane (c3), which reads only from the front (census: front). The drawn fault, a too-wide start (c2), also shows from the front.
plate.equipment: Seated hip adduction machine (composed, census R3): seat, back pad, footrests, two leg pads on the inner thighs just above the knees, side handles (c1). Floor line.
plate.start: Seated, back flat on the pad (c4); legs apart to a light inner-thigh stretch (c2); pads on the inner thighs above the knees, feet on the footrests, hands on the handles (c1).
plate.end: Thighs squeezed together until the pads nearly touch (c3); back still on the pad (c4).

checkpoints.label: Light stretch
checkpoints.what: Start only as wide as a light inner-thigh stretch.

checkpoints.label: Pads meet
checkpoints.what: Squeeze until the pads nearly touch.

checkpoints.label: Back on pad
checkpoints.what: Back flat against the pad, spine neutral.

mistake.what: Starting too wide: the legs are spread into a deep, forced stretch at the start.
mistake.why: Motra lists avoiding an excessive stretch at the start as its safety note. No source ranks how common it is.

tells.text: Only a light stretch at the start
Pads nearly touch at the end

setup.step: Sit with your back against the pad and feet on the footrests.
Set the thigh pads on your inner thighs, just above the knees.
Set the start width to a light stretch, not a deep one.
Pick a moderate weight and check the selector pin is secure.

posture.point: Back flat against the pad, spine neutral.
Start with only a light stretch.
Squeeze until the pads nearly touch.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Starting with the legs spread into a deep stretch.
handlingMistakes.fix: Set a narrower start: a light stretch only.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Using momentum to swing the legs together.
Weight too heavy to keep good form.

rows.means: The adductors are doing the work.

rows.fix: Stop; don't train it with an acute groin injury.

rows.where: Sharp stretch in the groin at the start
rows.means: Usually means the start is set too wide.

risks.risk: An excessive stretch at the start is the machine's main safety note.
Not for use with an acute hip or groin injury.

zooms.right: Legs open to a light inner-thigh stretch.
zooms.wrong: Legs forced wide into a deep stretch.

zooms.right: Back flat against the pad as the thighs squeeze.
zooms.wrong: Back peeled off the pad to swing the legs together.
